XP Power.why: Supplies high-voltage and application-specific power supplies designed into wafer-fab equipment (etch, deposition, ion implant, inspection, lithography) for all the key equipment manufacturers; semiconductor equipment orders rose 116% in H1 2026 as the fab investment cycle restarted.
XP Power.evidence: XP Power Q2 FY2026 (08-04-2026), CEO: 'XP is exposed across all steps in the manufacturing process, from lithography, deposition, etch, ion implant, and inspection, and with all the key equipment manufacturers.'

players.product: high-voltage and application-specific power supplies for semiconductor manufacturing equipment (etch, deposition, ion implant, inspection)

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 results: revenue GBP 109.1 million, up 2% in constant currency and down 2% at actual exchange rates (weaker US dollar), held back by the expiry of US export licences for RF sales into China; order intake GBP 167.2 million, up almost 55% in constant currency and 48% sequentially, with growth in every sector and region and Q2 stronger than Q1; group book-to-bill 1.53. Adjusted gross margin up 450 basis points to 45.9%; adjusted operating profit up 23% in constant currency to GBP 8.6 million (margin 7.9%); adjusted diluted EPS GBP 0.142 versus GBP 0.004; statutory profit GBP 1.1 million versus a loss of GBP 1.8 million. Industrial technology revenue up 9%, healthcare down 13%; North America up 3%, Europe up 6%, Asia down 11% on the exit from the China semi market. Net debt GBP 47.7 million, leverage 1.3 times.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 revenue GBP 109.1 million (+2% constant currency); orders GBP 167.2 million (+55%); adjusted gross margin 45.9%; adjusted operating profit GBP 8.6 million; book-to-bill 1.53

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: semiconductor manufacturing equipment orders rose 116% in H1 as the industry enters a new wafer fabrication investment cycle; some customers placed orders earlier on longer lead times to secure supply in tightening conditions, giving a record sector book-to-bill of 1.81. CEO: growth is both new business and market recovery, with wins in etch, deposition, ion implant and recently inspection; after a competitor in the high-voltage space had a business continuity issue in Q1, XP gained additional share with some key customers. CEO: XP is exposed across lithography, deposition, etch, ion implant and inspection and with all the key equipment manufacturers; AI-related investment is driving demand for more advanced semiconductor manufacturing capability, and customers are moving from standard products to application-specific, higher-power solutions.

The order book stands at GBP 174 million, including GBP 135 million of firm orders scheduled for delivery in the second half; CFO: H2 order book cover is probably slightly greater than in prior years, and the final outcome depends largely on how fast capacity can be expanded to convert the orders. Industrial technology orders rose 22% and healthcare orders 25% in H1, marking the end of destocking.
quarterly_data.figure: order book GBP 174 million; GBP 135 million firm for H2

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 guidance unchanged: the order book supports second-half revenue of at least GBP 135 million and full-year revenue of at least GBP 244 million, subject to prevailing tariffs (which could affect revenue but not profit); full-year effective tax rate 20%-25%; total capital spend including capitalised development GBP 25 million-GBP 30 million; leverage approaching one times by year end. Through-cycle targets: organic growth around 10%, adjusted operating margin around 20%, operating cash conversion around 85% of EBITDA, return on capital 20%, leverage 0-1x. CEO: confident XP can deliver double-digit organic revenue growth across the cycle.
quarterly_data.figure: H2 revenue at least GBP 135 million; FY2026 revenue at least GBP 244 million; capex GBP 25 million-GBP 30 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: lead times are in the five- to six-month region, slightly extended during Q2; underlying price increases (apart from tariff pass-through) contributed to H1 revenue and should contribute more in 2027. The overall supply chain is definitely tighter than 12 months ago, and component delivery delays in Q4 could push some deliveries past the balance-sheet date. Inventory was raised 29% to GBP 73.8 million, focused on critical high-use components.
quarterly_data.figure: lead times five to six months; inventory GBP 73.8 million (+29%)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: the Malaysia facility (total cost GBP 20 million, completed on budget) is complete, with first customer shipments expected in Q4 and full production starting in Q4; its ramp depends on the pace of qualification with key customers, and Vietnam is expected to drive most of the 2027 growth. Over 1,200 new staff were recruited and trained in Vietnam during Q2; H1 production-capacity investment was GBP 2.7 million (GBP 1.6 million Vietnam, GBP 1.1 million Malaysia), with the aim of raising Asia manufacturing line capacity by around 75% versus the first half.
quarterly_data.figure: Malaysia facility GBP 20 million; Asia line capacity +75% targeted; 1,200 new staff in Vietnam

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: XP has pulled out of supplying the Chinese semiconductor market directly - its RF export licences have expired and several key customers there were put on the US Entity List - and supplies them only indirectly through its key customers. CFO: H1 adjusting items relate mainly to the China factory closure and the decision to exit the RF market.
